title: Four levels, after GRADE (an example)
about: Four levels of certainty; randomised evidence starts high and observational low; five factors lower it and three raise it. Written after Guyatt et al. (2008), GRADE: an emerging consensus on rating quality of evidence and strength of recommendations, BMJ 336, 924-926, as an example. It is not GRADE's own text, and its rules for reading a synthesis (an interval that crosses zero, I² above one half and three quarters, Egger's test below 0.1 with ten studies or more, a pooled effect beyond a declared magnitude) are this example's.
text:
scheme after_GRADE
levels very_low low moderate high
start randomised high
start observational low
down risk_of_bias 2
down inconsistency 2
down indirectness 2
down imprecision 2
down publication_bias 2
up large_effect 2
up dose_response 1
up opposing_confounding 1
